text.p: Supertel Hospitality Inc said Tuesday it expects 1997 net income from operations of $3.85-$4.05 million, or $0.80-$0.84 per share.
For 1996 the company reported net income of $3.37 million, or $0.70 per share.

The company said 1996 earnings declined from 1995 levels due to "costs associated with an accelerated property development program, including higher depreciation and amortization and interest expense."
The company added, "We expect to resume our earnings growth in 1997."

Supertel said its seasonally slow first quarter will be below company expectations. "We now expect that 1997 first quarter earnings will be in the range of $190,000 to $290,000, or $0.04 to $0.06 per share," it said.
Revenues for the quarter were slightly softer than expected due to two factors, Supertel said.

"First, because we aggressively used introductory room rates to build our business in Texas, this gave us a lower average daily room rate. But, as a result of this promotional activity, we were able to build occupancy in Texas, which we expect to be approximately 10 percentage points higher in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the year-ago period.
"As of March 1, 1997, we raised rates in Texas, which should improve revenue per available room (REVPAR) in the state."
"Our first quarter was also impacted by the more seasonal nature of business in Wisconsin," it said. In 1996 Supertel acquired six properties in Wisconsin.

"With softer revenue contributions from Wisconsin and Texas in the quarter, it is hard to absorb the higher level of fixed costs associated with our expansion program, including real estate and property taxes, depreciation and amortization, and interest expense," Supertel said.

In addition, expense growth also exceeded revenue growth in some categories, it said. "We successfully increased our advertising and made broader use of our SuperStart continental breakfast to attract business," it said.
Supertel owns and operates limited-service lodging properties under the Super 8 and Comfort Inn names. The company has 59 motels, primarily in the Midwest and Texas.
